story.head: The Kraken’s edge in preventing dangerous shots
paras: The Blackhawks (6-14-2) lost 4-2 to Columbus on Thursday, while the Kraken (10-8-1) beat Vancouver 5-1 the same night. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Kraken fifth in the Pacific (tied for 23rd).

The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.318) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .393, and their goaltending has held them back. The Kraken’s record (.553) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.430), largely thanks to their finishing. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest), don’t block many shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (31st). Chicago has scored 2.45 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 4.05, the second most. The Kraken rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd), give up a lot of shots (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (31st). The Kraken have the edge over the Blackhawks on preventing dangerous shots.

Sam Rinzel (1 G / 13 A / 14 P in 21 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Frank Nazar (11 G / 2 A / 13 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brandon Montour (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 18 GP) isn’t far behind.

Spencer Knight (6-11-1 / .886 SV% in 18 GS) will likely start for Chicago. Seattle has two options in net: Philipp Grubauer (6-4-1 / .897 SV% in 10 GS) and Joey Daccord (4-4-0 / .872 SV% in 9 GS). Grubauer has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Daccord has a .934 save percentage in seven starts against the Blackhawks, well above his usual .903. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
